title: How an outbound call flows

nodes.label: Studio UI
nodes.note: Operator screens: Coach builder, Test and Refine scorecards, Playground, knowledge bases, campaign queue with live status, call history and analytics.

nodes.label: Your own system
nodes.note: Optional. Pushes contacts into a campaign with POST /api/v1/campaigns/:id/contacts and a bearer API_TOKEN. Extra fields become {{variables}}.

nodes.label: Routes + auth
nodes.note: middleware.ts redirects or 401s without a session. Auth.js signs in by shared password or Google, limited to ALLOWED_EMAILS. Every record is scoped by ownerId.

nodes.label: Webhook endpoint
nodes.note: POST /api/voice/webhook. Public, checked only by the X-Lyzr-Signature HMAC (timing-safe compare) and fails closed with a 503 if no secret is set.

nodes.label: SSE queue stream
nodes.note: GET /api/voice/queue/stream. Subscribes to an in-process EventEmitter and sends a fresh queue snapshot only when the campaign changes, with a 25s keep-alive ping.

nodes.label: Queue engine
nodes.note: calls/service.ts (tickStep, dialNext, reconcileCalls): picks the next contact by priority, calling window and attempt cap, uses dial_locks, then dials through Lyzr Voice.

nodes.label: 45s sweep
nodes.note: Started from instrumentation.ts when RUN_WORKER is not false. Ticks campaigns with voice work or due reschedules, firing scheduled calls and healing missed webhooks.

nodes.label: Post-call decision
nodes.note: Classifier result is validated, an opt-out phrase check can only tighten it, then the pure computeRecall function picks retry, callback, close or suppress.

nodes.label: Coach
nodes.note: server/coach: vertical-aware intake slots, script authoring, a word budget (soft 950, hard 1400) and compliance lines injected by code when the model omits them.

nodes.label: Test and Refine
nodes.note: server/testing: simulated callers, a conduct judge voted 3x, red-team scenarios, an optional real-audio test call, and improveScript with a regression check.

nodes.label: Knowledge base service
nodes.note: Creates Lyzr RAG collections, trains them from files, text, websites or Drive documents, tunes retrieval and attaches a KB to an agent.

nodes.label: Analytics + export
nodes.note: Reach and outcome funnels over call records, drill-down rows behind any number, and CSV or XLSX export.

nodes.label: MongoDB
nodes.note: Agents, campaigns, contacts (free-form fields), calls and transcripts, the call_queue and dial_locks collections, coach history, KB records and Drive tokens.

nodes.label: Lyzr Voice (LiveKit)
nodes.note: Runs the deployed voice agent. Provides outbound telephony, browser Playground sessions, transcripts and billing, and posts the transcript.ready webhook.

nodes.label: Lyzr Agent Studio
nodes.note: OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint hosting four text agents: Coach, Runner (simulated caller), Judge and Classifier. Created by scripts/setup-lyzr.mjs.

nodes.label: Lyzr RAG
nodes.note: Each knowledge base is a Lyzr RAG collection. The default vector store is Qdrant and the default LLM is gpt-4o-mini, both overridable by env.

nodes.label: Google Drive
nodes.note: Read-only OAuth for importing documents into a knowledge base, with connect, callback and disconnect routes.

nodes.label: Contact's phone
nodes.note: The person being called over the phone network.

flow: An operator starts a campaign. The queue engine picks the next contact by priority, calling window and attempt cap, and takes a dial lock in MongoDB.
It merges the agent config, campaign settings and the contact's variables and asks Lyzr Voice to place the call.
Lyzr Voice runs the agent on the phone call. Meanwhile the open SSE stream pushes queue snapshots to the browser.
When the call ends, Lyzr posts a signed transcript.ready webhook. The endpoint checks the HMAC before doing anything.
The app fetches the transcript and a classifier agent labels the outcome, intent and any opt-out. Code validates the result and a phrase check can only make an opt-out stricter.
computeRecall decides whether to retry, schedule a callback or close the contact. The queue advances to the next contact.
Secondary path: a 45 second sweep ticks campaigns that have scheduled calls due or calls whose webhook never arrived, so the queue keeps moving without a browser open.
Secondary path: before launch, the Coach writes the script and Test and Refine runs simulated and red-team calls against it with the Judge agent.
